final_message:
Blog slugs now keep the base letter of accented characters, so "Crème brûlée recipes" becomes `creme-brulee-recipes`. `npm test` passes, all 3 tests, including `test/blog-slug.test.js`.

The cause was in `vendor/slugify`, which deletes any character outside `a-z0-9`, so accented letters were dropped. `vendor/` is third-party code I'm not allowed to edit. Instead, `postSlug` in `src/blog/slug.js` now strips the accents (Unicode NFD normalization, then removing combining marks) before calling it.

`src/shop/product-url.js` also uses a slug. If it calls the vendored `slugify` directly, product URLs will have the same accent problem. I didn't change it.
